THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 05.12.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.M.C. 9986/2025 Shyamsundar vs State Of Kerala on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69843055/
1  2  2025:KER:94333  ORDER Dated this the 5th day of December, 2025
This is a petition filed under Section 528 of B.N.S.S, by the sole accused in Crime No.544/2025 of Maradu Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376(2)(n) of IPC and 66(E) of Information Technology Act.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused after promising to marry the defacto complainant,
sexually abused her, took her nude photographs and intimidated her and thereby he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, now the matter has been settled with the defacto complainant and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The petition was opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. On a perusal of the FI statement, it can be seen that the defacto complainant, after her divorce with the earlier husband, came in contact with the petitioner and thereafter on one day in October,
2018 at about 6 p.m., she accompanied the petitioner in his car and on the way he allegedly sexually abused her.
From the FI statement, it is further revealed that thereafter on more than one occasion also she accompanied the petitioner and on those days also she was allegedly raped by the petitioner.

2025:KER:94333 6. From the conduct of the defacto complainant in accompanying the petitioner again and again after the alleged sexual abuse, prima facie shows that the relationship was a consensual one.
Moreover, the matter has been settled with the defacto complainant and as such no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner.

7. The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions, submitted that the defacto complainant has given signed statement to the SHO, in tune with the affidavit filed by her in support of the Crl.M.C.
8.
In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioners in Crime No.544/2025 of Maradu Police Station, stands quashed under Section 528 of B.N.S.S. Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
